definitions.gloss: energizing; passing an electric current through something
definitions.explanation: Applying electric current to a device or circuit so that it becomes live, typically to power equipment on for operation or testing. Takes する to form a verb.

examples.japanese: ⟦{装置|そうち}→装置：03318_souchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{通電|つうでん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
{通電|つうでん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦ランプ→ランプ：11260_ranpu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{点灯|てんとう}する→点灯する：20211_tentousuru⟧。
examples.english: When you apply current, the lamp lights up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{配線|はいせん}→配線：07862_haisen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}して→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{通電|つうでん}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please check the wiring before turning on the power.

notes:
Refers to letting electricity flow into a circuit or appliance, typically to power it up or test it. Takes ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ to become a verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {通電|つうでん}⟦{確認|かくにん}→確認：00158_kakunin⟧: checking that current flows
- {通電|つうでん}⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧: a powered, live state
- {通電|つうでん}⟦{試験|しけん}→試験：01422_shiken⟧: an energization test

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{導電|どうでん}→導電：30048_douden⟧: electrical conduction — the property of conducting, not the act of switching on
- ⟦{停電|ていでん}→停電：03544_teiden⟧: power outage — a loss of electricity supply
